window_note: Rolling feed of deeply-researched picks (moneylines, totals, spreads, player/match props, and parlays) across the full confidence spectrum, refreshed hourly but only updated when something genuinely changed. Confidence tracks the specificity of the evidence. Only games that haven't started yet are included. Nothing here is ever a guaranteed outcome, however lopsided it looks.

reasoning: Buffalo (8-1, first in the NFL in points per game) hosts Miami (1-8, three straight losses); the Bills are a 16.5-point favorite with moneylines from about -1150 to -1700 (-1450 as of Nov 18), roughly 92-94% no-vig, and one model gives them 90%.

Injuries on both sides: the Bills have several players questionable, with Tyrell Shavers out (ACL) and Ar'maj Reed-Adams on IR; Miami has several questionable. NBC Sports leans Dolphins +16.5 on the spread, but that is a margin call, not a win call. I shaded to 91%.
Kickoff is 1:00 pm ET (18:00Z) at Highmark Stadium.

picks.matchup: Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs
reasoning: Kansas City is a 15.5-16.5 point home favorite with a moneyline near -1420 to -1600 (about 91-92% implied); one model gives the Chiefs 88% and projected scores run about 23-9 to 30-10.

Arizona starts rookie QB Carson Beck and has RB James Conner on IR, but the Chiefs are short-handed too: RT Jaylon Moore, RG Trey Smith (concussion protocol) and RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) were not expected to play and Travis Kelce has an ankle issue. Shaded to 89%.
Kickoff is 1:00 pm ET (18:00Z) at Arrowhead Stadium.

settled.matchup: San Antonio Spurs at Chicago Bulls
reasoning: Spurs are 9-2, second in the West, and have won nine straight, including 122-96 at Phoenix on Nov 9 when Victor Wembanyama had 40 points and 9 blocks; he is averaging 30.1 points and 11.9 rebounds. Bulls are 1-8, 14th in the East.

Spurs are without Devin Vassell (adductor) and Jayden Quaintance (knee), with Tobias Harris (calf) out or a game-time decision depending on the source. Bulls have Norman Powell day-to-day (shoulder) and Zach Collins day-to-day (illness).

The Bulls have won seven of the last 10 meetings, but the Spurs won the most recent one 129-114 on Mar 30. Posted moneyline is about Spurs -800 / Bulls +570 per FanDuel (roughly 87% no-vig), so the estimate is 86%.
Tip is 7 pm CT Wednesday Nov 11 at the United Center (01:00Z Nov 12).
Ohio State is a 11-12.5 point home favorite at Ohio Stadium (moneyline about -549 / +410, roughly 83% no-vig) and has won 11 straight against Northwestern.

Caveats: Ohio State (6-3, coming off losses) is without QB Julian Sayin and expected to start freshman Luke Fahey, with LG Luke Montgomery and WRs Phillip Bell and Brock Boyd questionable. Northwestern (6-3) is also without QB Aidan Chiles. The uncertainty at QB justifies shading to 76%.
Kickoff is noon ET (17:00Z) on FOX per multiple previews.
Clemson (6-3, 4-2 ACC) hosts Georgia Tech (2-7, 1-5) at Memorial Stadium; spread is about Clemson -13.5 (DraftKings) with a moneyline near -550 / +410, roughly 83% no-vig.
Clemson is without RB Gideon Davidson and WR Tyler Brown (ankle injuries), so I shaded the estimate below the market to 79%.
Kickoff is 12:30 pm ET (17:30Z) on The CW.
No. 4 Notre Dame hosts a 4-5 Boston College team at Notre Dame Stadium; the Irish are about a 30-point favorite (-28.5 to -31.5 across books).
Posted moneylines run roughly -4662 to -10000 and Kalshi has Notre Dame near 99%; capped at 94% since the payout is tiny and any single-game upset risk is nonzero.
Kickoff is 3:30 pm ET (20:30Z) on NBC/Peacock. I did not find a confirmed 2026 injury report for either side.
Georgia is 8-1 and ranked No. 1 at home at Sanford Stadium; Missouri is 6-3 and fell out of the AP Top 25.

Georgia injuries are minor to moderate: center Drew Bobo and DT Josh Horton are questionable, OLB Amaris Williams is out and RB Chauncey Bowens has been out since Oct 3. Missouri is without edge Langden Kitchen, RB Malae Fonoti, OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman. I could not confirm Georgia's 2026 starting quarterback.
Posted moneyline is about Georgia -750 / Missouri +525 (DraftKings, Nov 12), with Georgia -15.5 and other tables showing -714 to -1000; roughly 86% no-vig, so the estimate is 86%.
Kickoff is 3:30 pm ET (20:30Z) per the Week 11 schedule.
Virginia Tech is 6-3 (3-3 ACC) at Lane Stadium; Stanford is 4-5 (2-4 ACC) and is making its first trip to Blacksburg. Stanford's defense has allowed 199.7 rushing yards per game.
Posted moneyline is about Virginia Tech -700 on BetMGM, with the Hokies -15.5 to -17 and Kalshi at about 85%; the estimate is shaded to 83% because I found no confirmed injury report for either team.

Kickoff is 7:30 pm ET (00:30Z Nov 15) on the ACC Network per most sources; one Covers page lists 1:00 pm ET and an older Stanford page listed two options, so the start time is the majority-source value.
Jaguars (6-2) visit the Titans (1-7); Jacksonville is about a 10.5-point road favorite with a moneyline near -600 / +440 (DraftKings), roughly 84% no-vig. Kalshi and OG.com markets sit near 83-84%.

Most published picks (SI 31-13, Predictem 30-16) back Jacksonville; BetMGM is the only dissent, on the Titans spread. Titans RB Tyjae Spears and WR Carnell Tate are questionable; Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten and edge Travon Walker are also questionable. Shaded to 82% for the injury uncertainty and road-favorite variance.
Kickoff is 1:00 pm ET (18:00Z) at Nissan Stadium.

settled.matchup: San Antonio Spurs at Utah Jazz
reasoning: Spurs are about a 17.5-point favorite with a moneyline near -1640 / +920 (Bang the Book); FanDuel has -1786. OG.com prediction markets put San Antonio at about 94%.

Utah is badly short-handed: Bang the Book lists Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Nurkic, Hayes and Alexander out (Sportsmole instead calls Hayes a game-time decision, so that one is unresolved). I found no injury news on Wembanyama.

Capped below the market at 92% because a single NBA game can swing on rest or a late injury. Tip is 5:00 pm ET (22:00Z); sources disagree on which team is the listed home side, but the price is the same.

Boston is about a 9.5-point home favorite with a moneyline near -426 (Bang the Book) to -460 (Bleacher Report), roughly 81-82% no-vig; shaded slightly to 80% because only one preview covered this game in detail.

Orlando is listed without Paolo Banchero (ankle), Jonathan Isaac (knee), Noah Penda (hamstring) and Izaiyah Nelson (ankle), though that injury list comes from a single source and could change by tip-off. No Boston injuries were returned in the latest check.
The preview cites Boston's unbeaten home record and stronger scoring defense, but Orlando is on a three-game winning run. Tip is 7:00 pm ET (00:00Z Nov 17), which is 6:00 pm CT on Nov 16.
Western Michigan is a 14.5-point home favorite at Waldo Stadium (spread steady since open) with a moneyline near -675 / +490 (Bang the Book), roughly 86% no-vig; Polymarket also sits near 86%.
Shaded to 82% because both starting quarterbacks (WMU's Broc Lowry and EMU's Noah Kim) are reported dealing with injuries and I found no confirmed injury report.
Kickoff is 6:00 pm ET (23:00Z) on Nov 17 per two 2026 previews.
Ohio (7-3, 5-1 MAC) hosts Ball State (3-7, 2-4 MAC) at Peden Stadium; Ohio is favored by roughly 9.5-11.5 with a moneyline between about -355 and -450, roughly 78-82% no-vig.
Most previews pick Ohio (ATS.io 31-20, TheRx 31-14), though Bang the Book takes Ball State outright, and I found no confirmed injury details, so I shaded to 78%.
Kickoff is 7:00 pm ET (00:00Z Nov 18), which is 6:00 pm CT on Nov 17.

settled.matchup: Charlotte Hornets at Los Angeles Lakers
reasoning: Lakers (12-2, eight straight wins) host the Hornets (4-9) at Crypto.com Arena; moneylines range from -381 (DraftKings) to -578 (Bang the Book) and Polymarket has LA near 79%, so I used 82%.

Charlotte is without Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder, Moussa Diabate and Grant Williams. The Lakers are missing Austin Reaves (heel) and Walker Kessler, with Collin Sexton a game-time decision, so there is real injury risk on the Lakers side.
Tip is 11:00 pm ET (04:00Z Nov 18), which is 10:00 pm CT on Nov 17.

Miami (8-6) hosts Milwaukee (1-13, still seeking its first road win) at Kaseya Center; the Heat are about a 12.5-point favorite with a moneyline near -750 to -770 (roughly 87% no-vig), while prediction markets put Miami near 83%, so I used 85%.

Miami has Bam Adebayo (hip), Nikola Jovic (illness) and another player listed day-to-day, and Milwaukee is missing only Ousmane Dieng (finger). Sources disagree on streaks, and Fox Sports' page for this game is internally inconsistent, so I discounted it.
Tip is 7:00 pm ET (00:00Z Nov 19), which is 6:00 pm CT on Nov 18.

settled.matchup: New Orleans Pelicans at Oklahoma City Thunder
reasoning: Thunder are about an 11.5-12.5 point favorite at -499 to -525 (roughly 82-84% no-vig), and Covers' expert puts them near 88%; Sportsmole projects a 119-107 Thunder win.

reasoning: Oregon (No. 14) is a roughly 14-16.5 point road favorite with a moneyline between about -750 (Sharp Football Analysis) and -850 (Bleacher Nation), about 86-88% no-vig.

I shaded to 83% because Oregon is without QB Dante Moore (concussion, not expected back this season) and RB Jordon Davison, with Dylan Raiola at quarterback, and Michigan State is a 5-point-plus spread move from open (+13.5 to +16.5), so there is some injury and line-movement risk on the Oregon side.
Projections favor Oregon comfortably (Capper's 38-17, WagerTalk 27-14). Kickoff is 8:00 pm ET (01:00Z Nov 21), which is 7:00 pm CT on Nov 20.

settled.matchup: Sacramento Kings at Los Angeles Lakers
reasoning: Lakers are priced near -1040 / +670 (about 91% no-vig) and Covers' Polymarket-based figure is 86%, so I used 88%. The Lakers beat the Kings 116-103 on Nov 4 with Luka Doncic scoring 40.
Lakers are without Austin Reaves (heel) and Walker Kessler, but Sacramento has six players out or questionable (Raynaud, Simmons, Mogbo, Pedulla out; Achiuwa and Hunter questionable).
Tip is 10:00 pm ET (03:00Z Nov 21), which is 9:00 pm CT on Nov 20. Odds came from a single source (Bang the Book), and I did not find a current preview with a posted line.

Wake Forest (9-1, 6-1 ACC) is about a 20.5-21 point favorite at 3-7 Georgia Tech with a moneyline between -1450 and -1600 (roughly 93% no-vig); ESPN's FPI gives Georgia Tech 7.5% and AccuScore has Wake Forest at 92%.
Caveat: Georgia Tech just upset Clemson 20-6, and Wake Forest WRs E. Otieno and N. Carr are questionable; I found no complete injury list, so I shaded to 91%.
Kickoff is 12:00 pm ET (17:00Z) at Bobby Dodd Stadium on ESPN.
Liberty (9-1, unbeaten at home) is about a 17.5-point favorite over 4-6 Western Kentucky with a moneyline near -850 / +575; one preview has Liberty at 88%.
I found little injury information for either team, and Western Kentucky has two quarterbacks who both played last week, so I stayed at 85%.
Start time is a mild inconsistency: most sources list 1:00 pm ET (18:00Z) at Williams Stadium but one lists 12:00 pm ET, so I used 18:00Z.

Georgia (9-1) visits South Carolina (6-4, 4-4 SEC) at Williams-Brice Stadium as a 14.5-16.5 point favorite with a moneyline near -715 to -800; prediction markets sit at about 85-88% and ESPN Analytics gives South Carolina 13.1%.
South Carolina has 13 players on the SEC injury report, including several starters out and five questionable, though QB LaNorris Sellers is not listed. Rivalry games are volatile, so I stayed at 86%.
Kickoff is 7:30 pm ET (00:30Z Nov 22) on ABC per newer sources (one older Bleacher Report page lists 4:30 pm), which is 6:30 pm CT on Nov 21.
